problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 4},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $z+{x}^{2}=4$ in the first quadrant.
worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,dV={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}3x\,dy]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}3x\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}3x[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=4}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x(4-{x}^{2})\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/bcac3bb634fa04d2ccd4c3897f7b1db891a0b21eacfa96579f672b812fd92c07.png)

 

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}3x(4-{x}^{2})\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-{x}^{2}}3x(4-{x}^{2})\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3x(4-{x}^{2})[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-{x}^{2}}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3x(4-{x}^{2})(4-{x}^{2})\,dx \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-2x)(4-{x}^{2})^{2}\,dx \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{(4-{x}^{2})^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(\frac{0-{4}^{3}}{3}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(-\frac{64}{3}) \\  & =32\end{aligned}
$$
